standfirst: This issue covers OpenAI tightening GPT-6.2 usage limits, several ChatGPT demos you can try with a calendar or bank account, and a few skills worth testing.
digest: The one change that affects planning is OpenAI lowering usage limits on GPT-6.2. An OpenAI engineer says Astra now hits its cap 40% sooner and Sol 25% sooner. Claude Code and the Gemini API had smaller updates, covered below.

For a consultant, the useful clips this week are OpenAI's walkthroughs of Finances in ChatGPT and of a dot that watches projects while you are away. Both show agent-style work in a form a client can follow in a few minutes.

On the tools side, last30days and diagram-design are the easiest to try, though both need a Claude Code setup. Markitdown helps when you need to feed client documents to an assistant. Clients may also ask about the Photoshop warning from the New York Times.

items.title: OpenAI shows how a dot keeps work moving while you're away
items.summary: A user walks through prompts that have his dot watch projects, flag what needs attention and queue approvals. The prompts are in the description, so they are easy to copy.

items.title: Finances in ChatGPT: a beginner's walkthrough
items.summary: Covers linking a bank account, reviewing subscriptions and building a budget. Consumer-facing, but good background if clients ask about ChatGPT and personal data.

items.title: ChatGPT checks your calendar and drafts a note when plans change
items.summary: With a calendar connected, it proposes another slot and drafts the message to attendees. Takes a minute to try on your own calendar.

items.title: Tier list ranks the best AI models for coding
items.summary: Matthew Berman's opinionated ranking of current coding models. Useful for a quick view of how they compare, though the video carries a sponsor read.

items.title: Amateur astronomers use Codex and Astra to find possible exoplanets
items.summary: Two hobbyists searched public telescope data for dips in starlight. A clear example of non-experts using AI on open data; nothing to set up.

items.title: Hark Pro sorts an inbox, orders dinner and spots a double booking
items.summary: A hands-off test of a sponsored assistant handling email, a DoorDash order and a calendar check. Treat it as a demo, not a recommendation.

items.title: The AI Advantage flags ChatGPT updates worth knowing about
items.summary: A short clip on recent ChatGPT changes from a creator who covers AI tools. Quick to watch, though it also promotes a paid community.

items.title: OpenAI cuts GPT-6.2 usage limits, with Astra capped 40% sooner
items.summary: An OpenAI engineer says Astra now hits limits 40% faster and Sol 25% faster. Check team usage before promising clients a workload.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.329 warns where a folder's hooks come from
items.summary: Adds a trust dialog showing where hooks are declared, and lists scheduled tasks and /loop wakeups in /tasks. Mostly useful for security-minded teams.

items.title: Gemini API adds Tool Retrieval so agents can use hundreds of tools
items.summary: In preview, it lets an agent pick from many tools while spending fewer tokens. Aimed at developers, so ask an engineer before pitching it.

sections.title: Tools and skills you can use

items.title: diagram-design generates 52 types of editorial diagrams in HTML and SVG
items.summary: A skill for Claude Code and other coding agents that produces clean, self-contained diagrams. Handy for client decks, though it needs a coding agent installed.

items.title: last30days researches a topic across Reddit, X, YouTube and Hacker News
items.summary: An agent skill that gathers recent discussion on any topic and writes a grounded summary. Good for client prep; needs a Claude Code setup.

items.title: Microsoft's markitdown converts Office documents and other files to Markdown
items.summary: Makes client documents easy to feed to an AI assistant. It is a Python tool run from the command line, so a little technical comfort helps.

items.title: Academic Research Skills guide Claude Code from research to final draft
items.summary: A skill set that walks through research, writing, review and revision. Worth testing on a literature-heavy brief; needs Claude Code.

items.title: New York Times warns photographers off updating Photoshop over AI features
items.summary: The Verge reports the warning, and the Hacker News thread has 269 comments. A live example of clients worrying about AI in everyday software.

items.title: Golden State Warriors use Gemini for fan experiences and operations
items.summary: Google's partnership story covers the Warriors, Valkyries and Chase Center. Vendor-written, but a concrete sports and venue example to borrow from.
